claim.content: Justification of the candidate for an individual episode, reconstructed from contextual experimental findings.
claim.level_decision: Explicit iteration-1 choice: individual claim, retaining the documented contextual/individual ambiguity rather than silently generalizing.

nodes.content: pp.6–8: EEG/ECG and a classifier estimate high/low workload; training uses tasks similar to the application tasks. p.14: individual calibration.
nodes.epistemic_description: Mechanism described; no individual record recovered.

nodes.content: p.7: the authors cite a 70–95% classification range from previous studies.
nodes.epistemic_description: Background evidence; not a calibration of need or an accuracy estimate for the A-01 episode.

nodes.content: pp.13–15: 2×2 within-subject design; high/low task load. High load: 8.7 messages/min and five tasks; low load: 3.8 and four.
nodes.epistemic_description: Experimental design; task load is not individual cognitive workload.

nodes.content: p.15: high load impaired manoeuvre tracking (p=.01) and increased five NASA-TLX indices.
nodes.epistemic_description: Aggregate results; support for a risk of impairment in that scenario.

nodes.content: pp.8–9: PDA text is less salient; messages are immediately available; withdrawal requires lower workload, accumulated message reading, and confirmation.
nodes.epistemic_description: Mechanism and management conditions described by the source.

nodes.content: p.16: available mitigation improves count accuracy (p=.02) and manoeuvre accuracy (p=.01) under high load.
nodes.epistemic_description: Aggregate system comparison; not an isolated effect of a single component.

nodes.content: pp.17–18: situational awareness 30%→0%, p=.04; data from 5/8 participants because of recording failures.
nodes.epistemic_description: Observed cost; small sample and incomplete data.

nodes.content: p.16: mathematics response time 8.6→3.8 s, nonsignificant difference; accuracy unaffected; 7/8 participants under high load.
nodes.epistemic_description: Inference limit; neither a confirmed time benefit nor evidence of zero effect.

nodes.content: pp.8–9,13–14: message priorities assigned by the designer; priority tasks have equal importance.
nodes.epistemic_description: Documented origin of local priority; not universal authorization for compensation.

nodes.content: p.14: eight male volunteers without military experience. p.19: the authors interpret the balance as favourable during temporary overload.
nodes.epistemic_description: Limits on transfer and interpretation, not a validated sufficiency standard.

nodes.content: Dorneich et al. (2012), Considering Etiquette in the Design of an Adaptive System. Extracts transcribed from the A-01 documentary dossier; original PDF not re-audited in this iteration.
Support to preserve accuracy of priority tasks when incoming messages increase overload risk.
Published high task-load experimental context; no individual episode fabricated.
Divert lower-priority mission messages to immediately accessible PDA text; retain high-priority radio messages; recovery remains part of the candidate.
No mitigation under high task load.
Reported workload mechanism and task impairment make contextual support need plausible; no measured individual need.
Reduced competition for attention is a plausible contribution; reported effect belongs to the experimental package.
Improved count and manoeuvre accuracy under high load; package-level comparison.
